goal: Build me a small Python decision-model toolkit for applications that need quick structured decisions rather than generated paragraphs. A caller should provide shared state, a natural-language question and options defined at runtime, including Turkish labels; support binary, choice and ordered-level decisions. Return stable typed results with the original option identifiers, probabilities, selected answer and uncertainty information, and let several questions share one state without mixing their options. Keep the scorer replaceable so I can use deterministic scores in tests and later connect a local model. Validate malformed requests, duplicate options and invalid probabilities rather than silently repairing them. Provide a configurable fallback decision when confidence, margin or answerability is insufficient, and evaluation/calibration helpers that report honest metrics, including undefined cases. Preserve Unicode and stable serialization so another process can consume results, don't train or download anything merely to test the toolkit, and document a complete local example from request through scoring to response and fallback.

tasks.title: Specify typed request validation and lossless Unicode request serialization.
acceptance: Preserve the original Unicode state and option identifiers.
Reject insufficient options, duplicate ordinal levels and empty questions.

tasks.title: Specify logits, probability validation and numeric uncertainty output.
acceptance: Logits 2 and 0 map to approximately .880797 and .119203.
Selected identifiers and strict JSON serialization remain stable.
Margin and normalized entropy have concrete numeric values.
Reject negative, nonfinite, nonnormalized or mismatched probabilities.

tasks.title: Specify independent results for multiple questions sharing one state.
acceptance: Keep choice and binary option identifiers separate.
Equal logits give .5/.5 independently for both questions.

tasks.title: Specify confidence, margin and answerability gating with acceptance controls.
acceptance: Low margin, low confidence and insufficient answerability trigger their own reason codes.
A confident, answerable high-margin result requires no fallback and has no reasons.

tasks.title: Specify honest multiclass metrics and undefined-input failures.
acceptance: Macro-F1 includes the unpredicted class, yielding 1/3 in the provided two-label fixture.
For two correct .75-confidence predictions, NLL=-log(.75), Brier=.125 and ECE=.25.
Empty inputs and invalid bin counts raise ValueError.

tasks.title: Specify ordinal identities and deterministic declaration-order ties.
acceptance: Ordinal option IDs are the ordered level strings.
A uniquely highest medium score selects medium.
Tied nominal options choose zeta when it was declared before alpha.

tasks.title: Verify documented delivery and live UI/backend integration separately.
acceptance: Production model quality and calibration on real traffic remain separate empirical evaluations.
